title: Model Suite Hopscotch: Onboarding and Cross-Probe Safeguards
author: Ava Martinez
body:
Summary:

This playbook describes the "Hopscotch" onboarding pattern for model suites: a staged, workload-aware promotion pipeline that ensures cross-probe compatibility, quantization stability, and fast triage for regressions. The goal is to let model teams safely move a model from shadow validation to mixed-traffic canary to full promotion while preserving probe asset integrity and minimizing user-facing risk.

Audience:
- Model owners and applied ML engineers
- Eval engineers and probe stewards
- Release engineers and SRE oncall

Context and motivation:
- We maintain multiple models and variants (float, q8/q4_mixed, pruning variants, KV-cache-friendly builds). Each variant can interact differently with prompt families and the KV cache, leading to emergent regressions. The Hopscotch pattern provides deterministic gates and probe reuse rules that reduce duplicate evaluation work and improve rollback confidence.

Key concepts:
- Model Suite: a logical group of related artifacts (e.g., model-v1, model-v1-quant-q4, model-v1-pruned).
- Probe Asset: a curated prompt or slice used for continuous evaluation and sentinel checks.
- Hopscotch Steps: discrete promotion phases (Shadow, Lightweight Canary, Traffic Canary, Promotion).
- Cross-Probe Safeguards: rules that ensure probes remain valid across quant/variant changes.

Onboarding gates (summary table):
| Gate name | Minimum checks | Telemetry pass threshold | Responsible role | Timebox |
|-----------|----------------|--------------------------|------------------|---------|
| Shadow validation | 10k probe runs (slices) + privacy gating | 95% slice-level fidelity | Applied ML owner | 48h |
| Lightweight Canary | 1% production traffic, heatmap checks | 98% critical-slice fidelity, latency within 1.2x baseline | Release engineer | 24h |
| Traffic Canary | 5–10% traffic with mixed tenants | No critical regression, APDEX >= 0.96 | SRE/Platform | 72h |
| Promotion | Full traffic roll | Continuous monitoring active; rollback hooks tested | Product/Owner | Rolling |

Detailed procedure (step-by-step):
1) Preparation (Model owner)
   - Create a Model Suite manifest (see manifest example below).
   - Tag variant-level quant profiles (e.g., q4_mixed_v2) and list compatible prompt families.
   - Register probe assets in the Probe Registry with a reuse tag and ownership.

2) Shadow validation (Applied ML / Eval harness)
   - Run the model variant against the shadow probe set (10k sample) in an isolated eval mesh.
   - Required outputs: fidelity delta per slice, embedding drift, top-5 token divergence, latency P50/P95.
   - Blocking rule: any critical-slice fidelity delta > 6% (see fidelity buckets) triggers a stop.

3) Lightweight Canary (Release engineer)
   - Deploy variant to a tiny pool behind a shadow router (no user exposure) or 1% routed traffic flagged as canary.
   - Execute focused probes: top 20 critical slices and functioncall cases used by product features.
   - Run quant-stability quick checks (token coherence check with synthetic seeds).

4) Traffic Canary (SRE)
   - Expand routing to 5–10% following tenant-aware sampling to avoid tenant-correlated regressions.
   - Use the Telemetry Contract to evaluate cost/latency regressions: token-cost delta, KV cache hit rate, batching efficacy.
   - Hold for the timebox or until sample sizes pass statistical checks.

5) Promotion and hardening
   - If canary metrics meet SLOs, promote in waves (25%, 50%, 100%) with automated revert hooks.
   - Run full-suite evals nightly for first week post-promotion and mark probe artifacts as "freshly-validated".

Hopscotch-specific artifacts and examples:

Model Suite manifest (YAML snippet):
{code:yaml}
name: payment-assistant-suite
variants:
  - id: v3.0-fp32
    quant_profile: none
    compatible_probes: [payment_intent_slices, pii_redaction_slices]
  - id: v3.0-q4m
    quant_profile: q4_mixed_v2
    compatible_probes: [payment_intent_slices, pii_redaction_slices]
  - id: v3.0-pruned
    quant_profile: pruning-medium
    compatible_probes: [payment_intent_slices]
owners: ["payments-nlp@redwood.com"]
{code}

Probe registration example (CLI):
- Register a probe:
  rwd-evalctl register-probe --name payment_intent_slices --owner payments-nlp --tags critical, pii, kv-sensitive --sample-size 3000

Quant stability quickcheck (JSON expected output example):
{code:json}
{
  "probe": "payment_intent_slices",
  "fidelity_delta": 0.012,
  "token_divergence_p95": 0.048,
  "kv_hit_delta": -0.002,
  "coherence_score": 0.984
}
{code}

Quality thresholds and telemetry (normative):
- Fidelity buckets:
  - Critical slice: pass if fidelity_delta <= 0.02
  - Important slice: pass if fidelity_delta <= 0.05
  - Noncritical slice: pass if fidelity_delta <= 0.10
- Latency: P95 must be within 1.3x baseline for Lightweight Canary, 1.15x for Traffic Canary.
- Token-cost: no more than +7% token-cost at Traffic Canary without product approval.
- KV cache hit rate: within -3% of baseline during canary.

Cross-probe safeguards (rules):
- Probe compatibility mapping: all variants must declare compatible probes. If a new variant lacks compatibility for a probe tagged "critical", the probe is excluded from automated promotion and must be evaluated manually.
- Reuse rule: do not duplicate probes across suites. Use reuse tags and reference canonical probe ids.
- Aging rule: probes older than 18 months must be revalidated before use in Shadow validation.
- Annotation contract: when a probe fails due to model change, annotate with failure class (regression, noise, tokenization) and link to root-cause issue.

Regression triage integration (fast-path):
Trigger conditions for fast-triage:
- Any critical-slice fidelity_delta > 0.06 in Shadow or Canary.
- APDEX drop > 0.10 within a 10-minute window.
- Sudden KV cache hit loss > 5% correlated with a quant variant.

Fast-triage steps (ordered):
1) Pager to oncall + owner (SRE + model owner).
2) Isolate variant and switch traffic to fallback model (automated).
3) Run the Regression Forensics checklist: seed reproduction, token-level diff, prompt-context sensitivity scan, quant-bit sensitivity sweep.
4) If suspected quant-failure, run back-to-back against float baseline and alternative quant profile.
5) Produce an interim incident note and tag the probe with "regression-escrow".

Ownership and escalation matrix:
- Model owner: responsible for manifest, probe compatibility map, and remediation plan.
- Eval steward: maintains the Probe Registry and runs scheduled revalidations.
- Release engineer: executes Canary steps and verifies rollout gates.
- SRE oncall: responders for telemetry triggers; empowered to rollback with automated hooks.

Observability checklist (must be configured before Lightweight Canary):
- Per-probe fidelity dashboards (slice-level heatmaps).
- Token divergence histogram by slice.
- KV cache hit rate and eviction rate.
- Cost-per-request (tokenized) and APDEX.
- Canary vs baseline request tracing (trace id level).

Common failure modes and recommended mitigations:
- Symptom: coherent responses but hallucinated entity values on critical slices.
  Mitigation: run functioncall determinism probe and compare top-3 outputs; if divergence, revert to float and open a model-tuning ticket.
- Symptom: P95 latency spike only in quant variant.
  Mitigation: ensure kernel selection compatibility (see [eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling]). If still present, limit batch size on the canary pool and re-evaluate.
- Symptom: isolated tenant regressions during Traffic Canary.
  Mitigation: pause expansion and run targeted tenant shadow with per-tenant probes.

Retention and artifact lifecycle:
- Probe artifacts: retain raw probe runs (inputs + model outputs) for 90 days by default; metadata and annotations retained indefinitely.
- Quant profiles: immutable once used in a promotion. New profiles must be created for any tuning changes and tied to a new variant id.

Appendix: checklists and templates
- Pre-shadow checklist:
  - Manifest submitted and reviewed.
  - Probe owners assigned.
  - Telemetry dashboards smoke-tested.
  - Rollback playbook validated.

- Incident note template (consolidated):
  - Incident id:
  - Model suite / variant:
  - Triggering metric and timestamp:
  - Immediate mitigation actions:
  - Root-cause hypothesis:
  - Next steps and owners:
